redFirst.basis: regression mode, expectRedFirst false; the CI failure did not reproduce on this machine (3 planted tables locally vs 4 in CI, mac fonts; letter-spacing 0.02-0.08em widening also did not reproduce it), so no red was watched for the hostile leg

outcome.technical: shell.css: added `.tablewrap{overflow-x:clip}` after the existing break-word table rule (break-word kept, so P123.90 title behaviour is unchanged). clip makes no scroll container (sticky thead keeps working); the 52rem media rule (overflow-x:auto) and the print rule (overflow:visible) come later in the cascade and still win. Pinned by new case u14kt in test_render_report.py (rule present once, ordered before both overriders); selftest all pass. Re-rendered examples/acme-store/acme-store-audit.html, docs/index.html (via examples/report.sh) and docs/demo-large.html; check-rendered-artifacts OK. check-report-interactive passes on example, docs/demo-large.html and the live plan render. Rejected on mac measurement: `anywhere` on tables (title words split mid-letter at 833px), with nth-child(2) min-widths 11/16/20rem (still splits numerics or widens the document). CAVEAT: I could not reproduce the CI failure (4th planted data table, Linux fonts), so the fix is unproven against it; it enforces the invariant structurally (a table cannot widen the document above the scroll breakpoint) at the cost that a table wider than its column is clipped, not scrolled, between 52rem and where it fits. acme-store-audit.md only changed its generated stamp; I reverted it. Screenshots not recaptured.
outcome.descriptive: Tables can no longer widen the document above the scroll breakpoint, keeping break-word titles; the CI-only hostile-content failure was not reproduced locally.

claims: claims: u14kt asserts presence and order of the CSS rule only, not browser behaviour; browser behaviour was measured by check-report-interactive on three pages locally, none of which reproduced the CI failure before the fix.
